Strong start to 2019: total revenue +20% to $14.5M, North America +41% to record $11.4M; ex-China continuing ops +35%.
China royalty restructuring with Qifeng finalized; $12.2M note receivable recognized as other income, driving GAAP net income of $11.7M ($0.20/share).
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $878K vs $2.1M loss in Q1 2018.
Aggressive drug-channel expansion: CVS national rollout to 7,500+ stores, new Rite Aid at 2,300+ of 3,000 - ~11,000 total drug locations.
Target expanded to 1,200+ stores (4 SKUs), going to 1,500; persistent out-of-stocks from warehouse replenishment limits, prompting DSD transition talks.
Big Geyser agreement (post-quarter) called 'one of the strongest and most transformative agreements to date' - NYC's largest independent non-alcoholic distributor, 20,000+ locations.
New DSD agreements secured with Anheuser-Busch, Keurig Dr. Pepper, MillerCoors network partners.
International revenue declined ~$900K - $1.3M China reduction (model shift) partly offset by 20% European growth on new flavor launches.
Europe characterized as 'stabilization' not expansion; capital deliberately directed to North America given lean team.
Cash fell to $2.8M from $7.7M on inventory build (peak levels for summer season) and China-related marketing settlements.
Gross margin held flat at 39.5%; near-term pressure expected at low end of 39%-low-40s range due to heavier new-DSD-launch promotions.
Share count jumped to ~57.2M from conversion of ~6M Carl DeSantis preferred shares - all preferred stock removed from balance sheet.
RTDs drive ~85% of revenue; powders secondary; SKU 'billboard effect' quantified (2->4 SKUs can quadruple account sales).
Energy-category transformation toward better-for-you alternatives opening retailer doors; management confident and growth-focused.
Big Geyser, Target/CVS trends, new customers
What Big Geyser distributor means for NYC, update on Target/CVS trends, any other major customer worth highlighting.

Big Geyser addresses NYC distribution gap (reliance on wholesalers/warehouses); official kickoff next week. Target at 1,500 stores but still out-of-stocks - DSD transition discussions, another flavor, cold availability in back half. CVS national with 3 flavors; Rite Aid opened drug channel; Walgreens talks underway. More marquee accounts in convenience/grocery to be announced.
Update on co-packer picture and how revised setup benefits the company during peak selling season.
Inventories at highest levels, strategically built for pipe orders and summer season. Solidified Refresco relationship; 4 active co-packers, ample supply for 2019, building network for 2020+.
More on the Nordic region turnaround and strategy for other parts of Europe.

Nordics had strong Q1 on Peach Vibe launch; 2017-18 downturn appears stabilized. Beyond Nordics, focused on North American expansion given lean-team resources; China royalty model frees capital; delivered $800K+ positive adjusted EBITDA.
How many powder pack flavors are out and current distribution channels.

Launched cranberry lemon and coconut late 2018 (alongside orange, wild berry). Distributed mainly in health/vitamin specialty and health clubs; integrated into smoothies (doing well at Smoothie King). RTDs remain focus (~85% of revenue).
How to model international ex-China for the full year, noting easy Q2 comp off last year's $0.77M.

Break international into China (in line with royalty model, ramping with launch-cycle volumes) and Europe (stabilization to normalized levels, strong ACV but limited expansion as capital goes to North America).
Share-count jump, China note modeling, margins
Source of share-count jump to ~57.1M, how to model China note gain/interest, and margin outlook.

Share jump primarily conversion of ~6M Carl DeSantis preferred shares (cap table cleaned up). China note gain one-time; going forward royalty revenue plus ~$90-95K quarterly interest income (currency-translation effects). Margins targeted 39%-low-40s with co-packer leverage, but low end near-term on new-DSD-launch promotions.
China volume and Big Geyser rollout cadence
Whether China unit volume was up or down vs Q1 2018, and how the Big Geyser rollout (20,000 locations) plays out in 2019.

Declined to give unit volumes (not historically disclosed); revenue growth volume-driven at consistent pricing/allowances, China drop purely model-shift recognition. Big Geyser first phase targets key accounts (grocery, drug, 7-Eleven), then backfills - 'a journey,' not immediate 20,000-location authorization.
Given Big Geyser's tough-negotiator reputation, would gross margin on Big Geyser volume be below corporate but worth it?
Pushed back - Big Geyser margins expected consistent with other distributors (Big Geyser approached Celsius); mutually beneficial partnership with no expected margin deterioration.
Market share, ACV, and SKU billboard effect
In-store market share for stores in 12+ months, and how much adding SKUs boosts market share.

Overall ACV/market share low (single digits) as Celsius journeys into new channels (drug/mass new for 2019, no 12-month data). Convenience ACV rose to 10.8% with high-30s growth. Quantified billboard effect: 2->3 SKUs nearly doubles account sales, 2->4 SKUs can quadruple.
How competitive dynamics are evolving (Dr. Pepper zero-cal energy entry, Amazon's own energy brand) and effect on retailer conversations.

Innovation leading category; shift to better-for-you alternatives opening doors. Competition increasing (Amazon, Reign, Bang, C4) but Celsius differentiated by authenticity born in diet/sports nutrition and science. Retailers more open than ever, helping secure DSD partners.
